run.question: I have a slow query on the 'app-191-profile' index. Use the profile option to analyze this query and tell me the query type used: {"wildcard": {"message": "*timeout*"}}

report.summary: The query {"wildcard": {"message": "*timeout*"}} was profiled against the single index app-191-profile (1 shard, 6 documents, green) with the non-removable time filter on the mapped date field timestamp over 2026-11-20T05:17:03Z to 2026-11-21T05:17:03Z. In Elasticsearch query-DSL terms this is a wildcard query on the text field message, and the profile's Lucene-level name for the rewritten clause is MultiTermQueryConstantScoreBlendedWrapper with description "message:*timeout*", nested inside a BooleanQuery inside a ConstantScoreQuery next to an IndexOrDocValuesQuery on the timestamp range. The profiled run matched 3 documents in took=25 ms with 0 failed shards and timed_out=false, so the reported slowness was not reproduced on this 6-document index. That a leading-wildcard rewrite is what makes this query shape expensive at scale is a hypothesis; this dataset does not demonstrate it. Authorized target for this Run is m0-otel-20260909; app-191-profile is an index within that target, not a separately queryable target ref.

claims.text: Index app-191-profile exists as a single open green index with docs.count=6 and store.size=7.1kb on target m0-otel-20260909, and its mappings define message as text, status as keyword and timestamp as date.

The profiled search on index app-191-profile for {"wildcard": {"message": "*timeout*"}} succeeded with status ok: total.value=3 (relation eq), took=25 ms, shards total=1 successful=1 failed=0, timed_out=false, one backend summary returned.

The profile's query breakdown for shard [IlTWoknGQqy7nP5jTkKk2g][app-191-profile][0] lists for description "message:*timeout*" type MultiTermQueryConstantScoreBlendedWrapper (time_in_nanos 253468, build_scorer 238650 ns), nested under a BooleanQuery (time_in_nanos 1168746) that also holds IndexOrDocValuesQuery(indexQuery=timestamp:[1795151823000 TO 1795238223999], dvQuery=...), all wrapped in a ConstantScoreQuery (time_in_nanos 1544552, rewrite_time 174939).

The same profile lists a separate TermQuery described as "message:timeout" (time_in_nanos 34184, create_weight_count 1, next_doc_count 0) in the shard's query list; the profile does not show where that clause originated in the request.

The tool applied a non-removable time filter on field timestamp spanning 1795151823000 to 1795238223999 (2026-11-20T05:17:03Z to 2026-11-21T05:17:03Z); the returned source samples sit at source_start_at=2026-11-21T05:11:00Z and source_end_at=2026-11-21T05:15:00Z.

No slowness was observed in this run: the profiled execution finished in took=25 ms with query-phase collector time_in_nanos 4099578 and no timed-out or failed shards, so the reported slow query was not reproduced on this index.

The MultiTermQueryConstantScoreBlendedWrapper rewrite of the leading-wildcard pattern *timeout* is a plausible source of expense on a large message field, since such a pattern cannot be resolved to a single indexed term; this index holds only 6 documents, so the profile timings here do not demonstrate that cost.

If the wildcard shape must stay, consider querying a keyword, normalized, n-gram or reverse-token field, or a match query on message, so the clause can use term-level lookups instead of a leading-wildcard multi-term rewrite; validate on a dataset that reproduces the slow timing before changing production queries.

gaps: The index holds only 6 documents, so the profile timings (query phase ~4.1 ms, took=25 ms) cannot show why the query is slow on the dataset where the slowness occurs; no production-scale profile was collected.
The profile covers one shard only (total=1), so per-shard skew in a multi-shard production index is unknown.
The origin of the separate TermQuery "message:timeout" entry in the profile is not explained by the profile output and remains unknown.
The asserted slowness was not reproduced in the authorized window; the change_history integration is not available in this Run, so changes to the index or its query pattern could not be checked.
An earlier attempt without time_field failed with INVALID_PARAMS (TIME_FIELD_REQUIRED); that error view is not citable as fact and is noted only as the reason time_field=timestamp was used.
Index-level entity name app-191-profile is not a separately addressable target in this Run; all evidence is attributed to target m0-otel-20260909.
next_steps: Re-run the same profiled wildcard query against the full-size or live index (or a representative snapshot) to capture realistic shard timings.
Identify the callers that issue {"wildcard": {"message": "*timeout*"}} and assess whether the pattern can be narrowed or moved to a keyword/n-gram field.
